I have no idea how to solve this issue, so I'm just spitballing here. Some of these are horrible ideas, but hey, they're ideas.

  • Honestly, I haven't seen any mention of how they should be used since I got here. We need a page similar to https://www.reddit.com/wiki/reddiquette, and it needs to be pushed in your face, and frequently, at least early on, until people catch on.

  • To downvote(or at least occasionally), have a box where you can type a reason for the downvote. Occasionally offer random users the ability to review some of said downvote reasons(With the posts in question), and either mark that they're valid reasons, or that the user is just downvoting people who disagree with him. Warn them or remove downvoting ability if they're being shitty and using it wrong often enough(Similar to League of Legend's tribunal system).

  • ONLY if combined with some other system to figure out if people are using voting correctly, weight votes so that votes from people who vote correctly are worth more to a posts position, or make votes from abusers straight up not count.

  • Implement some kind of Altar of Literacy-esque test before users are able to (down)vote, to make sure they know how voting should work. If they fail, make them wait some amount of time before being able to retake it. This is probably the most harmless thing to implement.

  • Again, ONLY if combined with another system to make sure people are using voting correctly in the first place, you could semi-automate checking new users to see if they're using votes correctly by checking how often they agree with other users who are confirmed to have been using votes well. The issue here being, if good users change habits, or if they aren't confirmed as good users first, this could just as easily enforce bad voting habits.
